item.title: Charlotte Marathon to honor deceased runner with bib tribute
item.description: The Charlotte Marathon will honor avid runner Lance Sotelo during this Saturday’s races by placing his silhouette on every runner’s bib. Sotelo was killed in a hit-and-run crash in the NoDa neighborhood in January. Sotelo competed in the Charlotte Marathon last year, finishing fifth in his first marathon. This weekend, his partner, James Holt, will run the 5K to honor Sotelo’s memory and dedication to running. Channel 9 reporter Evan Donovan spoke with Holt about preserving Sotelo’s memory following the crash. Holt reflected on the difficult period since losing his partner. I got to get in a run, no matter what, every day.” Marathon organizers announced the tribute in a social media post, revealing that each runner’s bib on Saturday will be adorned with Sotelo’s silhouette. Holt said seeing the gesture meant a lot to him. “Wow, that was so cool,” Holt said. “And you know, he’s going to be a part of everyone that’s running out there, so that’s going to be really special.” Holt added his thanks for the honor. “To have him honored as part of it is just unbelievable,” Holt said. “I just can’t thank them enough.” Regarding the legal outcome, a judge sentenced the driver who hit Sotelo, Q’Laundra Hood, to 30 days in jail in September. The court also ordered Hood to pay restitution to Sotelo’s family. Channel 9 will broadcast race highlights and runner stories in a Charlotte Marathon special airing at noon on Sunday.

item.title: Falcons Cut Nick Folk For Jake Moody In Bold Roster Shake-Up
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Atlanta Falcons made a definitive roster move on Wednesday by releasing kicker Nick Folk and signing Jake Moody from the Baltimore Ravens’ practice squad. The roster move signals a clear shift in strategy as the team prepares to face the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, November 15. The organization is prioritizing long-term stability over short-term comfort, a choice that reflects the reality of a 3-6 season. Head coach Kevin Stefanski addressed the media on Wednesday to explain the logic behind cutting a captain. “The truth is in football, you lose guys due to injury, you can lose them due to a trade or due to guys getting cut,” Stefanski said. He emphasized that the team must adapt to these changes immediately. The Falcons gained three draft picks through recent trades involving safety Jessie Bates and center Ryan Neuzil, further indicating a focus on building for the future. Why The Move Makes Sense Now Nick Folk was a reliable presence for the team until a missed 38-yard field goal in the third quarter of the loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, November 8. Folk, who is 42 years old, had previously made 107 consecutive field goals from inside 40 yards. His season record stands at 13 of 18 on field-goal attempts. The Falcons are replacing him with 26-year-old Jake Moody, who was activated from the practice squad after he made a 53-yard field goal in the rain against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Stefanski expressed confidence in the new direction. “Decisions that are made for our football team are always in the best interest of our football team,” he stated, according to CBS News . The coaching staff says Moody has a skill set that matches the team’s direction. The team made the move to improve roster depth for the remainder of the season. Leadership Changes Across The Roster Roster turnover also affects positions beyond the kicker. The team also traded center Ryan Neuzil to the Ravens, leaving a hole in the offensive line that Corey Levin will fill. “Obviously, love ‘Neuz’,” Stefanski said regarding the veteran center. “Great person. Just felt like this was an opportunity for our football team and comfortable and feel good about Corey Levin stepping in.” Levin joined the team after following his former offensive line coach, Bill Callahan, from the Tennessee Titans. Defensive captain Jessie Bates was also traded to the Jaguars for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. New leaders will be named as the players who finished second to Bates and Folk in the team’s captain vote, according to CBS News . The Falcons have lost four of their last five games but remain in a competitive division. “We’re excited about this game in front of us,” Stefanski said. The team faces a difficult challenge to avoid a ninth straight losing season while playing in the weak NFC South.

item.title: UK Fans Travel Far To Cheer For Chicago Bears And Caleb Williams
item.description: Matt Marton-Imagn Images They are showing up in person, wearing the gear, and passing the torch to the next generation. The Chicago Bears organization made this shift official in October with their first-ever UK Grand Tour. The team visited all four nations during a three-week trip to connect with supporters. Bournemouth, Cardiff, Leeds, Glasgow and Belfast saw events attended by over a thousand fans. Tom and Joseph Bond traveled from Newport to Cardiff with Joseph’s eight-month-old daughter, Eleia. They wanted to introduce her to the fandom she is being raised with. Tom recalled seeing the event on social media and asking his brother to join. He views his role as an uncle as a duty to make her a true Bears fan. From Cubs to Bears Joseph did not love the sport until a decade after Tom started watching around 2006. Prior to switching football teams, he was a fan of the Chicago Cubs during the 2010s. He decided to stick with the Chicago franchise and join his brother in their support. “I thought I might as well stick with the team in Chicago, and now I’m a big Bears fan too,” Joseph said. The two brothers have bonded closer over the last ten years through their shared love of the team. Anticipating further community growth, they credit the leadership of coach Ben Johnson and quarterback Caleb Williams. Strangers now recognize each other on the street. Tom noted that people walk around wearing Bears hats and gear. He once spotted a man with the same hat in a supermarket. They exchanged a silent nod of recognition. “I saw a guy with the same Bears hat on a random day in the supermarket, and we both gave each other the little nod. Yeah, it’s a bit of a unique thing,” Tom said. New Faces, Old Nicknames Dale Edwards arrived at Cardiff Castle dressed to honor the late Mike Ditka. He wore a No. 89 jersey and painted his nails in the same design his coach uses. Dale only became a Bears fan six years ago when he bought a random NFL jersey with a friend. The Walter Payton jersey he picked up matched his childhood nickname, “The Bear.” He said the nickname came simply because he “was big and hairy.” Before that moment, he had no interest in the sport. “I wasn’t interested in football,” Dale said. He knew nothing about the game until a friend changed his mind. Now he is part of a growing group that travels across the UK to support the team. The fans believe the team is turning a corner after some rough years. They are eager for the NFL season to return. The last two years have been incredible for the franchise, and this season looks to be good. The Bears defense has also shown it can win games on its own. The unit recorded seven sacks in just two games after trading for Jeffery Simmons. This performance helped the team beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 27-24 on Sunday, Nov. 8 at Soldier Field. The defense allowed only two third-down conversions on 12 attempts during that game.

item.title: Mike Brown’s Ref Rant Hits Home After Knicks’ Free-Throw Woes
item.description: David Richard-Imagn Images Mike Brown did not hold back after the Knicks fell to the Cavaliers on Wednesday night. The coach called the free-throw discrepancy “pretty alarming” following the 115-107 loss at Madison Square Garden. New York took just 11 free throws while Cleveland earned 25, a gap that hurt the Knicks in the final possession count. Brown pointed out that Jalen Brunson played nearly 35 minutes without a single trip to the line. “Jalen plays 34 minutes or almost 35 minutes and he has zero free-throw attempts,” Brown said. “That’s pretty alarming. I’m not sure how or why it’s that way.” Why the Whistle Matters Brown noted that the Knicks used to enjoy a massive advantage in free throws, but that edge vanished on Wednesday. He admitted the bad calls were part of the reason his team lost the possession battle against a strong opponent. James Harden was the main culprit for the Cavs, shooting as many free throws as the entire Knicks roster combined. Harden finished with a game-high 32 points, including clutch buckets that sealed the win. Per the New York Post , this was the first time since February 11 last year that Brunson failed to attempt a free throw. The star guard has to contend with physical defense, but his coach thinks a zero‑point total in a game of this length is unacceptable. Brown said he just hopes for a better whistle when playing good teams because winning is already hard enough. Brunson and the Bench React Jalen Brunson tried to stay focused despite the frustration. He told reporters he has to control what he can control and keep moving forward. Miles McBride also felt the sting of a missed call late in the game when his shot was blocked. McBride thought it was a goaltend, and he said the guys on the bench agreed with his take. Karl-Anthony Towns had a solid night with 21 points and 11 rebounds, matching a franchise record for double-doubles to start a season. But the rest of the starting lineup struggled to score. OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges, and Josh Hart combined for just 22 points on poor shooting. Bridges played only 17 minutes and sat out the entire fourth quarter as the team looked to others for help. The Takeaway The loss snapped a four-game winning streak for New York, and the officiating did not help their cause. “He’s a tough matchup for anybody in this league. You gotta tip your hat to him,” McBride said of the veteran star.

item.title: UCLA Basketball Sets Program Record With 69-Point Blowout
item.description: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images UCLA men’s basketball delivered a historic defensive performance on Wednesday night, defeating Arkansas-Pine Bluff 106-37. The 69-point margin of victory set a new program record, surpassing a trio of 65-point blowouts from decades past. Ninth-ranked UCLA held the Lions to just nine points in the first half while forcing 30 total turnovers. This smothering display came five days after the Bruins scored over 100 points in a previous blowout win. Coach Mick Cronin deployed a “nuisance press” using long, athletic forwards to disrupt ball movement. The strategy worked immediately, making clean passes nearly impossible for Arkansas-Pine Bluff. The team recorded 19 steals in the game, with Eric Dailey Jr. grabbing four and Jaylen Petty, Joe Philon III, and Azavier Robinson each adding three. The Record-Breaking Margin The 69-point difference broke a record that stood since 1967, when the roster included Lew Alcindor, now known as Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. UCLA outscored the Lions by 42 points at halftime alone, a lead not seen since at least the 2012-13 season. Arkansas‑Pine Bluff made just three field goals in the first half and missed all nine of their three‑point attempts. The defense was so effective that the opponents were forced into constant contact. Nearly every effort by the Lions proved futile against the relentless pressure from the Bruins. Since the 1975-76 season, no UCLA team with a 3-0 record has surrendered fewer points than this one, which equals a 1983 contest where Howard was limited to nine first-half points. Disrupting the Opponent’s Flow Coach Cronin explained that the goal was to stop teams from getting into their preferred offense. He noted that the press forces opponents to worry about breaking the zone before they can even organize. This leaves them with little time to run their usual plays. “What we’re trying to do with that is disrupt the other team’s flow,” Cronin said, according to the New York Post . Joe Philon III and Nikola Kusturica are the forwards positioned at the attack’s front in this plan. Because of their length, teams struggle to reverse the ball or complete passes with high efficiency. Cronin added that he does not have to fight players to believe in this style of play. “I don’t have to fight them to believe in extra passes, execution, the art of real basketball versus the art of dribbling 50 times and doing nothing,” Cronin said, “so it makes it fun as a coach.” Player Reactions and Future Outlook Trent Perry, the UCLA point guard, scored 11 points and dished out a career-high 11 assists. He described the feeling after the game as being “Speechless.” Perry admitted the specific outcome was not the main goal but accepted the result. “I mean, that wasn’t something that we’re aiming for, but we’ll take it,” Perry said. item.description: Nations League | Italy 3-1 France: Pio Esposito puts Azzurri top to end Bleus curse Francesco Pio Esposito scored twice, though brother Sebastiano missed a penalty, along with Davide Frattesi’s goal as Italy beat France 3-1 at San Siro to go top of their Nations League group. Les Bleus failed to win only once under Zinedine Zidane, the 1-1 draw with the Azzurri in Paris , and visited San Siro without Inter’s Marcus Thuram, Juventus defender Pierre Kalulu, Roma midfielder Manu Koné, Kylian Mbappé, Ousmane Dembélé, Aurelien Tchouameni, William Saliba, Jules Koundé, Maxence Lacroix, Maghnes Akliouche and Esteban Lepaul. Gianluca Mancini, Nicolò Zaniolo, Moise Kean and Mattia Zaccagni were among those unavailable for the Nazionale, who looked to the Esposito brothers upfront. item.title: Skattebo Admits Giants Wanted Better Back After Trade Talks
item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images The New York Giants went hunting for elite help before the trade deadline, but Cam Skattebo knows why the team looked elsewhere. He admitted his own numbers have not been good enough to stop the front office from making calls. The team tried hard to land big names but walked away with their current roster intact. Now the Giants must decide if Skattebo can carry the load against Washington on Thursday night. Honest Self-Reflection Skattebo did not make excuses when asked about the team’s search for a new running back. He told reporters he would be skeptical if his own backfield was averaging 60 yards a game without breaking big runs. “I would be skeptical, too, if my running back was going for 60 yards a game and not really exploding out,” Skattebo said. He knows the league moves fast and he is still learning how to play at this level. His current stats show a player who has not yet found his rhythm in the NFL. Skattebo remains convinced he can rank among the league’s most perilous running backs, even though his language has been harsh. That belief matters, but it does not change the fact that the Giants wanted more production. The team looked at Indianapolis Colts star Jonathan Taylor before pulling their offer. According to Heavy.com , the Giants reached out to the Falcons regarding Bijan Robinson. A Short Leash for Skattebo John Harbaugh is not afraid to bench players who struggle, and Skattebo knows his job is on the line. The Giants tried to acquire help because Skattebo’s role was not secure. If he does not step up, the coaching staff will turn to backup options immediately. The team missed the chance to add a vet, so the pressure now falls entirely on the players already in the building. Skattebo has to prove he is the answer for a team with playoff hopes. He missed the last game against Philadelphia due to a hamstring injury but returned to practice on Tuesday. The Giants will need him healthy and ready for the matchup in New Jersey. In seven games played this season, he accumulated 418 rushing yards along with two touchdowns. That total is not what a first-place team expects from its lead runner. The Giants were big-game hunting, but they did not close any deals. One Game to Prove It Following the trade deadline, Dan Duggan of The Athletic posted on his official X account Wednesday that the Giants were clearly hunting for major deals. They wanted a player who could change the game, but they settled for who they had. Skattebo will play in the upcoming Thursday night game. He needs to show he can explode for big gains and carry the offense. On Sunday morning, Adam Schefter noted that many individuals are questioning the Giants. The team did not make a move and will rely on its current group. The Giants will play the Washington Commanders at MetLife Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026.

item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. item.title: Bears Must Bench Bradbury To Fix Line Before Bye
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears sit at 7-2 and hold the top spot in the NFC North, yet their offensive line is cracking under pressure. Fans saw the struggle firsthand during the nail-biting 27-24 win over Tampa Bay on Sunday night. Pressure up the middle was constant, and the communication between the guards and center looked shaky. The team cannot afford these mistakes as the schedule gets tougher. A change is needed before the bye week ends. The center position has become the clear weak link on the line. Garrett Bradbury has been solid at times, but he cannot handle the job of calling out protections. He lacks the lateral quickness and strength needed to win at the point of attack. He frequently missed free rushers. It is consistently costing the offense by forcing Caleb Williams into immediate pressure or killing the run game. The rookie Logan Jones offers a better path forward for this team. Why Jones Is The Right Move Logan Jones was selected in the second round of the 2026 NFL draft. He stands as the highest drafted offensive lineman for Ryan Poles since Darnell Wright. Competing immediately means a second-round pick must contribute sooner rather than later. Earlier this season, Jones excelled in his limited reps versus the Atlanta Falcons. He was seen sealing off his man downfield and winning a few pass-blocking reps. While he is still learning, he is ready to step in. Bringing in Jones gives the line a fresh start. The team also needs Kyle Monangai to return from injury to help the running game. These fixes arrive at the perfect time thanks to the upcoming bye week. Yahoo Sports reports that Chicago Bears fans confront the week’s cliché “the bye week is coming at the perfect time.” The team is struggling with injuries, and this roster shuffle could be the key to a deep playoff run. A solid line protects the quarterback and opens up the run game. Winning Requires Better Protection Despite the Bears winning remarkably against the Buccaneers, weekly reliance on last-minute field goals to fix costly mistakes is impossible. Caleb Williams threw a career-high four interceptions in that game. Just two involved throwaways that failed to reach the sideline. The coaching staff must help him improve his decision-making. Devin Bush was awesome against Tampa with nine tackles and two passes defensed. The defense stepped up when the offense stumbled. Even with the win, the team faced a tough challenge. Injuries leaving big question marks compounded Rome Odunze’s case of the drops for the Bears. Near regulation’s end, Burden took a helmet-to-helmet hit and suffered a concussion. Prior to that hit, he logged seven catches totaling 97 yards along with one touchdown. The running backs are banged up, to say the least. The Bears need a productive and restful bye week to correct these issues.

item.description: Italy end France's unbeaten run and go top; England reach knockouts The fifth round of the UEFA Nations League kicked off on Thursday (12) with four matches. item.title: First-year soccer coaches look to guide teams to state championships
item.description: Dylan Martin is in his first season as head coach for Averill Park boys' soccer. (Stephen Weaver) Twenty-two years ago, Holli Mulholland won a state championship in her first season as head coach of the Shenendehowa girls' soccer team. She looks back on that run with pride - and one regret. "I probably could have enjoyed that a little bit more," Mulholland said. This week, Shenendehowa is one of 10 Section 2 boys' and girls' soccer programs competing in the state semifinals. Three of those programs have first-year coaches aiming to do what Mulholland did in her first season. The Bethlehem girls (Scott Geis), Averill Park boys (Dylan Martin) and Greenville boys (Jared McAneny) are each led by first-year head coaches. Each inherited a program with its own history and a different set of expectations. For Mulholland, she took over a Shen program built by Jan Federice, who was inducted into the New York State Soccer Hall of Fame in 2021. Federice won 277 games at Shen and shared a state title in 1992. Over 17 years, she won nine Section 2 championships and made six appearances in state title games. "I remember that (2004) season like it was yesterday," Mulholland said. "Partly, because I was so young and had taken over a program with a storied tradition of excellence. I remember thinking, 'Do everything in your power every day to give the kids the best experience you can and maintain that tradition of excellence.' "Sometimes, perceived pressure is the worst part of pressure, right?" she said. "The self-inflicted pressure. I certainly felt that." Her response was tunnel vision. "I remember just taking it one day at a time," she said. "Just sticking to those goals every single day, and trying to build the culture within the team." She said a new coach's early success is rarely only his or hers. Earlier coaches laid the groundwork. Players put in year-round club work. A team culture was ready to welcome someone new. The 2004 state final provided Mulholland with a lesson she still teaches her players today. Shenendehowa played that game without Ashley Moore, whom Mulholland called "arguably our best" player. Moore, who later played at the University of North Carolina, had left for a U.S. national team training camp after Shen won the state semifinal. Her absence set the stage for an unlikely hero in Deana Semenza, who hadn't played in Shen's postseason run. Semenza came off the bench and scored the game-winning goal in the state final. "We talk a lot about that story, about understanding your role, being willing to accept your role in the team," Mulholland said, "and how your role changes as the games and season continues. "I called her name to go in the game and she went sprinting down the sideline, started to warm up, came back in. item.description: Harry Kane was given a special shirt by Prince William and Peter Shilton before kick-off [Getty Images] "It's great when fairytales come true," England boss Roy Hodgson said after 21-year-old Tottenham striker Harry Kane scored 79 seconds into his international debut back in 2015. "Let's hope it's the start of a good and long England career for him." Eleven years on, Kane made his 126th appearance for his country and became the most-capped men's player in Three Lions history when England played Croatia in the Nations League at Wembley on Thursday. His record-extending 92nd England goal came from the spot in their 2-1 win. Peter Shilton, who served England as a goalkeeper, won 125 caps between 1970 and 1990. Shilton was part of a presentation to Kane with a special framed England shirt before kick-off. "It's not about me - it's about the team," said Kane beforehand. "I love coming to every England camp, I love playing every game and representing the country in the best way possible." Kane, 33, has gone through every emotion playing for his country. He fought back tears after missing a penalty in the World Cup quarter-final defeat by France in 2022, and sang Wonderwall with fans following the win over Croatia at this summer's World Cup - which he labelled one of his "favourite ever moments" in a Three Lions shirt. London-born Kane is the boy who grew up in Chingford to captain his country, become England's record goalscorer and win the 2026 Ballon d'Or. Now the Bayern Munich striker has made more appearances than any other man in England's football history. "He wins the Ballon d'Or, and deservedly so, and in the next game for England he gets the all-time record with 126 matches," England boss Thomas Tuchel said about Kane when announcing his squad last week. "Thursday is a deserved occasion to celebrate an extraordinary player." Kane: The England fan Long before Kane made his first senior appearance for his country in a 4-0 Euro 2016 qualifying win over Lithuania at Wembley, he was an England fan. Aged 12, he remembers the heartache of going out on penalties to Portugal in the quarter-finals of the 2006 World Cup under Sven-Goran Eriksson and failing to qualify for Euro 2008 under Steve McClaren.
